Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

himself pronoun

also by himself, to himself, he himself

classical

Publ. B 21: Bis vincit quī sē vincit in victōriā.
Publ. I 44: sibi tum īrāscitur

suī, sibi, sē (sēsē)

pronoun, reflexive: genitive suī, dative sibi, accusative and ablative sē; the same for every gender and number

himself (as object), referring to the subject

The reflexive refers to the subject of its clause: quī sē vincit, who masters himself. It has no nominative. “With himself” is sēcum. In reported speech it stands for the speaker: cujātem sē esse dīceret, where he would say he (himself) was from.

Other words

  • ipse — himself (for emphasis: he himself, in person, of his own accord)

    pronoun, intensive: genitive ipsīus, dative ipsī, declension · classical · Publ. Q 69: Quī sē ipse laudat, citō dērīsōrem invenit.; Liv. 22.2.10: ipse Hannibal

    Stresses the person: ipse Hannibal, Hannibal himself. With the reflexive it agrees with the subject when it stresses the doer, quī sē ipse laudat, who praises himself (no one else praises him); with the object when it stresses the object, sē ipsum fēlīcem facit (Lewis & Short, s.v. ipse).

Examples

  • Bis vincit quī sē vincit in victōriā.

    He wins twice who masters himself in victory.Publ. B 21

  • Īrātus, cum ad sē rediit, sibi tum īrāscitur.

    The angry man, when he comes back to himself, is then angry with himself.Publ. I 44

  • Quī sē ipse laudat, citō dērīsōrem invenit.

    Whoever praises himself soon finds someone to laugh at him.Publ. Q 69

  • Patiēns et fortis sē ipsum fēlīcem facit.

    The patient and brave man makes himself happy.Publ. P 37

  • locō herbidō ut quiēte et pābulō laetō reficeret bovēs et ipsum fessum viā prōcubuisse

    in a grassy spot, to rest his cattle with quiet and rich pasture, and that he himself, tired from the road, lay downLiv. 1.7.4

  • sēcum esse sēcumque, ut dīcitur, vīvere

    to be with oneself and, as they say, to live with oneselfCic. Sen. 49

See also he, herself, itself, themselves, oneself, myself.
